description: A composite group: a data table (Table 9) plus three optical micrographs labelled (a), (b), (c). The table is headed "Composition (wt%) | Hardness (Hot-rolled [HV] | Temperature [°C] | Tempered [HV] | Inter-lamellar spacing)" with two rows: 12Al-10Mn-1C (hot-rolled 401 HV, 800 °C, tempered 399 HV, "Wide") and 9Al-10Mn-1C (hot-rolled 273 HV, 600 °C, tempered 439 HV, "Narrow"). Panels (a-c) are optical micrographs, each carrying a 400 μm scale bar, showing banded/lamellar microstructures elongated along the rolling direction. (a) shows fine horizontal striations with alternating light and darker bands; (b) shows coarser dark elongated lamellae/pearlite-like colonies on a lighter matrix; (c) shows a finer, more mixed equiaxed-plus-lamellar field with many thin dark lamellae and a few dark cracks along the bottom edge. Taken together the group links the hardening response to inter-lamellar spacing: the 9Al-10Mn-1C alloy tempered at 600 °C with narrow spacing (273 → 439 HV) shows strong hardening, whereas 12Al-10Mn-1C at 800 °C with wide spacing essentially retains its hot-rolled hardness (401 → 399 HV).

observations.observation: Table 9 lists two compositions, 12Al-10Mn-1C and 9Al-10Mn-1C, with hot-rolled hardness of 401 HV and 273 HV respectively.
For 12Al-10Mn-1C the table gives tempering temperature 800 °C, tempered hardness 399 HV and inter-lamellar spacing 'Wide'.
For 9Al-10Mn-1C the table gives tempering temperature 600 °C, tempered hardness 439 HV and inter-lamellar spacing 'Narrow'.
The caption states that Table 9 reports the hardening effect and the inter-lamellar spacing.
Three optical micrographs labelled (a), (b) and (c) each carry a 400 μm scale bar.
All three micrographs show microstructures banded/elongated along one direction, consistent with a rolling direction.
The citing text states that 9Al-10Mn-1C alloys treated at 600 °C, with fine lamellae featuring short inter-lamellar spacing, showed significant hardening effects (Table 9).
The citing text states that the two last-mentioned microstructures kept the same hardness as their respective hot-rolled variants instead of being strengthened by the high amount of carbides.
